title: benchhand rule list (flow/<name>.celpolicy, restricted cel-policy), provisional
description: Provisional: one rule-list file, flow/<name>.celpolicy, in the restricted cel-policy profile of ADR-0020 (github.com/cel-expr/cel-policy): a name and one rule with one first-match match block. The profile has no variables, no aggregate, no nested rule and no other cel-policy field, explanation and imports included. The first choice whose condition holds gives its output. Every choice but the last has a condition, and the last has none, so every list gives a value. The pinned cel-go tool compiles each list before load into one checked expression of the rules bundle. It refuses a conditional last choice, an excluded feature and a result type other than its kind's; the schema checks the rest of the shape. The file doesn't say which list it is: the reference to it in flow.yaml, or in a policy contribution, carries its kind and rules_version. The kind sets the type of every output. checks_by_iteration: list(string), the check ids in run order, with a conditional check concatenated as a CEL ternary; [] is its no-match value. dispatch: string, a handler id, or its no-match value "unknown", which the host records as UNKNOWN coverage, never a pass. fidelity: string, the form-check fidelity "F0" to "F3", or its no-match value "none", which only a contributed list gives. rigor: list(string), the messages of the requirements the record doesn't meet under the project's rigor policy, ending in []. The slot type is string, so the compiler accepts any string a fidelity or dispatch output gives, computed ones included. The Phase 2 evaluator checks the kind's result against its domain: a fidelity outside F0 to F3, and a dispatch handler id that no handler has, is out of the domain, and the evaluator records it as UNKNOWN with a finding that names the value, never as a pass. policy/contribution.schema.json says how the lists of one kind combine

match.output: ["regulated rigor refuses a flow profile that turns a check off"]
